title: Spectral sequences and convergence, part II — the standard constructions and their products
summary: The standard spectral sequences of homological algebra built inside the convergence language of SpectralSequencesAndConvergence: the two spectral sequences of a double complex for both totalisations with half-plane convergence, comparison and acyclic assembly; horseshoe and Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions, right derived functors on D⁺ compared with the classical ones, and the two hypercohomology spectral sequences with their duals; the composition theorem and the composite-functor spectral sequence of a complex; balancing of Tor, universal-coefficient, Künneth and change-of-rings spectral sequences; pairings of exact couples, filtered complexes and double complexes; and the Bockstein spectral sequence with its higher Bocksteins, limit page and convergence.

layers.title: Double complexes and their two spectral sequences

targets.name: HomologicalComplex₂.totalProd
targets.statement: For a double complex K : HomologicalComplex₂ 𝒜 (up ℤ) (up ℤ) in a preadditive category with the products over the antidiagonals, the product total complex Tot^Π(K) has degree-n term ∏_{p+q=n} K^{p,q}, and the component of its differential with target K^{p,q} (p+q = n+1) is d₁ ∘ π_{p−1,q} + (−1)^p d₂ ∘ π_{p,q−1}. The direct-sum total complex Tot^⊕(K) is Mathlib's HomologicalComplex₂.total for the shape up ℤ.

targets.name: HomologicalComplex₂.columnSpectralSequence
targets.statement: For a double complex K and Tot(K) ∈ {Tot^⊕(K), Tot^Π(K)}, the column filtration F_I^p Tot(K) is the subcomplex of the columns of index ≥ p; the first spectral sequence ′E(K) is the base §5.1 spectral sequence of (Tot K, F_I); the second spectral sequence ″E(K) is ′E(K.flip) with abutment transported through the flip isomorphism, whose transported filtration is the row filtration F_II. Then gr^p_I Tot(K) ≅ (K^{p,•})⟦−p⟧, ′E_1^{p,q} ≅ H^q(K^{p,•}) with ′d_1 = H^q(d₁), ′E_2^{p,q} ≅ H_I^p H_II^q(K), ″E_1^{p,q} ≅ H^q(K^{•,p}) with ″d_1 = H^q(d₂), ″E_2^{p,q} ≅ H_II^p H_I^q(K); both are functorial in morphisms of double complexes.
hypotheses: Tot(K) exists (HasTotal for Tot^⊕, or the products for Tot^Π)

tests.name: first_quadrant

targets.name: HomologicalComplex₂.columnSpectralSequence_convergesStrongly
targets.statement: (a) If every antidiagonal of K has finitely many nonzero terms, both ′E(K) and ″E(K) converge strongly (base §3.2) in every degree to H^*(Tot K) with finite filtrations, and every position stabilises; Hⁿ(Tot K) lies in every weak Serre class containing ′E_r^{p,q} for all p, q and some r (stacks-012K Lemma 25.3 (4); base §5.3), and in every weak Serre class containing ′E_r^{p,n−p} for all p and some r from which every position of total degree n stabilises (base §§1.3, 3.4); similarly for ″E(K). (b) If 𝒜 has countable coproducts and exact sequential colimits and for every n there is b(n) with K^{p,n−p} = 0 for p > b(n), then ′E(K) converges strongly to H^*(Tot^⊕ K); dually ″E(K) when K^{n−q,q} = 0 for q > b(n). (c) If 𝒜 is in the class of base §7.4, for every n there is a(n) with K^{p,n−p} = 0 for p < a(n), and ′E(K) is regular, then ′E(K) converges strongly to H^*(Tot^Π K); dually for ″E(K). Regularity holds when for every n there is p₁(n) with H^{n+1−p}(K^{p,•}) = 0 for p ≥ p₁(n).
hypotheses: (b): HasCountableCoproducts 𝒜, HasColimitsOfShape ℕ 𝒜, HasExactColimitsOfShape ℕ 𝒜
(c): 𝒜 in the class of base §7.4 (countable products and coproducts, CountableAB4Star, exact sequential colimits, lim-acyclic epimorphic towers); §7.4 is used for this class only
the antidiagonal bounds stated in each case

targets.name: HomologicalComplex₂.acyclic_total_of_exact
targets.statement: Tot^⊕(K) is acyclic (𝒜 as in 1.3(b)) if its columns are exact and K^{p,n−p} = 0 for p ≫ 0 in every degree n, or its rows are exact and K^{n−q,q} = 0 for q ≫ 0; Tot^Π(K) is acyclic (𝒜 as in 1.3(c)) if its columns are exact and K^{p,n−p} = 0 for p ≪ 0, or its rows are exact and K^{n−q,q} = 0 for q ≪ 0; Tot(K) is acyclic in any abelian category with finite antidiagonals and exact columns or rows. Augmented forms: for an exact 0 → M → A_0 → A_1 → ⋯ of complexes, M → Tot^⊕(A) is a quasi-isomorphism (𝒜 as in 1.3(b)); for an exact ⋯ → A_1 → A_0 → M → 0, Tot^Π(A) → M is one (𝒜 as in 1.3(c)).
hypotheses: the exactness and antidiagonal vanishing stated
the class of 𝒜 of 1.3(b) for Tot^⊕ and of 1.3(c) for Tot^Π

targets.name: InjectiveResolution.horseshoe
targets.statement: (a) For a short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 of bounded-below complexes in 𝒜 with enough injectives and an injective resolution A → I₁, there are injective resolutions B → I₂, C → I₃ and a degreewise split short exact sequence 0 → I₁ → I₂ → I₃ → 0 compatible with the augmentations, vanishing in negative degrees when A, B, C, I₁ do; for objects, given resolutions of A and C, the middle can have terms I₁^n ⊕ I₃^n. (b) Given a morphism (f₁, f₂, f₃) of short exact sequences of objects, a short exact sequence of resolutions 0 → R₁ → R₂ → R₃ → 0 of the source, a degreewise split short exact sequence of injective resolutions 0 → I₁′ → I₂′ → I₃′ → 0 of the target, and chain maps α : R₁ → I₁′ over f₁, β : R₃ → I₃′ over f₃, there is μ : R₂ → I₂′ over f₂ restricting to α and inducing β.

tests.name: twisted_middle

tests.name: off_diagonal_needed
tests.statement: Target horseshoe transported by φ(u, v) = (u + h(v), v), h a family I₃^n → I₁^n; for the source differential d(u, v) = (d₁u + t(v), d₃v), φd − dφ = ((hd₃ − d₁h)(v), 0), so the identity is a chain map between the middle resolutions exactly when h is a chain map, while μ = φ always is. Instance: split 0 → ℤ/2 → ℤ/2 ⊕ ℤ/2 → ℤ/2 → 0, I₁ = I₃ = (ℚ/ℤ →(×2) ℚ/ℤ), t = 0, h = id in degree 0 and 0 in degree 1: d₁h − hd₃ = ×2 ≠ 0, the transported degree-0 differential is (u, v) ↦ (2u − 2v, 2v) against (2u, 2v). For h = id in both degrees the differentials agree, but the transported augmentation (a, c) ↦ (ε₁a + ε₃c, ε₃c) differs, so the identity still does not lie over f₂.

targets.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedPlusObj
targets.statement: For additive F : 𝒜 → ℬ with 𝒜 having enough injectives, RⁿF(X) := Hⁿ(F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus X) for X ∈ DerivedCategory.Plus 𝒜, and RⁿF(A) := RⁿF(A[0]). (i) RⁿF(A) ≅ (F.rightDerived n).obj A naturally in A and F; (ii) for K → T a quasi-isomorphism into a bounded-below complex of injectives, RⁿF(K) ≅ Hⁿ(F(T)); (iii) Hⁱ(X) = 0 for i < a implies RⁱF(X) = 0 for i < a, RⁱF(A) = 0 for i < 0, F(A) → R⁰F(A) is an isomorphism for all A iff F is left exact, and Hⁱ(RF(τ_{≤a}X)) ≅ Hⁱ(RF X) for i ≤ a; (iv) long exact sequences, δ-functor; (v) for F left exact, Leray's acyclicity lemma: a bounded-below complex of F-acyclic objects computes RF.
hypotheses: F left exact in (v) and in the R⁰ clause

targets.name: CochainComplex.CartanEilenbergResolution
targets.statement: For K with K^p = 0 for p < a in 𝒜 with enough injectives, a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution is a double complex I with ε : K → I^{•,0} such that I^{p,q} = 0 for p < a or q < 0, each column I^{p,•} with ε^p is an injective resolution of K^p, and the horizontal cycles, boundaries and cohomology of I (complexes in q, with the induced augmentations) are injective resolutions of Z^p(K), B^p(K), H^p(K). Such resolutions exist; their rows split; Tot(I) is an injective resolution of K; chain maps lift to morphisms of resolutions compatible with the augmentations and inducing lifts on columns, cycles, boundaries and cohomology.

targets.name: CochainComplex.bocksteinExactCouple
targets.statement: For a commutative ring A, f ∈ A and a cochain complex M of A-modules with f injective on every term, the Bockstein exact couple has D^{s,t} = H^{s+t}(M), E^{s,t} = H^{s+t}(M/fM), i = multiplication by f, j = reduction, k = connecting morphism of 0 → M →(f) M → M/fM → 0, of degrees (−1,1), (0,0), (1,0); the Bockstein spectral sequence is its base §6.1 spectral sequence. It is periodic in (s,t) ↦ (s+1, t−1); E_1ⁿ = Hⁿ(M/fM) with d_1 the connecting morphism of 0 → M/f →(f) M/f² → M/f → 0; it is isomorphic to the base §6.3 couple of M[1/f] filtered by F^s = f^sM.

locator.where: line 136–150, Example 2.3; stacks-more-algebra line 12960–13006 (§97, Bockstein operators) and line 13013–13014 (footnote 18); mccleary2001 Ch. 10 (uncertified)

tests.statement: M = ℤ →(×p) ℤ, f = p: k(1) = [1] ∈ ℤ/p, j([1]) = 1, d_1 = +1, an isomorphism.

tests.name: torsion_free_cohomology
tests.statement: M = ℤ[0], f = p: k = 0, every d_r = 0, E_r^0 = ℤ/p for all r.

tests.name: torsion_needed
tests.statement: M = ℤ/p[0], f = p: multiplication by p is zero, 0 → M → M → M/pM → 0 is not exact, no couple.

targets.name: CochainComplex.bocksteinSpectralSequence_limitPage
targets.statement: For M, f as in 6.1 and r ≥ 1: Z_{r+1}ⁿ = k^{−1}(f^r H^{n+1}(M)), B_{r+1}ⁿ = j(Hⁿ(M)[f^r]), Z_∞ⁿ = k^{−1}(⋂_r f^r H^{n+1}(M)), B_∞ⁿ = j(Hⁿ(M)[f^∞]); 0 → (f^{r−1}Hⁿ(M)) ⊗ A/f → E_rⁿ → (f^{r−1}H^{n+1}(M))[f] → 0 is exact; d_r[x] = [β_r(x̃)] for a lift x̃ ∈ Hⁿ(M/f^r); if Hⁿ(M)[f^∞] = Hⁿ(M)[f^a] and H^{n+1}(M)[f^∞] = H^{n+1}(M)[f^b] the sequence stabilises in degree n from page max(a,b)+1 with E_∞ⁿ ≅ H̄ⁿ ⊗ A/f; with Hⁿ(M)[1/f] filtered (exhaustively) by f^s H̄ⁿ, gr^s ≅ H̄ⁿ ⊗ A/f, and the canonical comparison gr^s ≅ ker k/B_∞ ⊆ E_∞ is an isomorphism in total degree n iff ⋂_r f^r H^{n+1}(M) ∩ H^{n+1}(M)[f] = 0, in which case it is a weak convergence structure (base §3.2), a convergence structure when moreover ⋂_s f^s H̄ⁿ = 0.

locator.where: line 147–168, Example 2.3 (higher universal-coefficient sequences and the limit page for finite type over ℤ); hatcher-at line 13330–13337, Proposition 3E.3; mccleary2001 Ch. 10 (uncertified)

api.name: CochainComplex.bocksteinSpectralSequence_multiplicative
api.statement: For a DGA M the pages carry pairings with d_r a derivation (5.2; may-primer line 288–294, Example 4.3).

tests.name: z_mod_pr
tests.statement: M = ℤ →(×p^r) ℤ: E_s⁰ = E_s¹ = ℤ/p for s ≤ r, 0 for s > r; d_1 = ⋯ = d_{r−1} = 0, d_r an isomorphism, E_{r+1} = 0, matching H¹ = ℤ/p^r; stabilisation from page r + 1. The representative of 1 ∈ E_r⁰ is the cochain u = 1 ∈ M⁰, not a cocycle of M (du = p^r) but one modulo p^r, with w = 1: k(1) = p^{r−1}[1] and d_r(1) = β_r(1) = 1.

tests.name: unbounded_torsion
tests.statement: M = ⊕_{k≥1}(ℤ →(×p^k) ℤ): E_r⁰ = ⊕_{k≥r} ℤ/p ≠ 0 for every r but E_∞⁰ = 0, consistent with H⁰(M)[1/p] = 0.

tests.name: weak_convergence_fails
tests.statement: M = ℤ → ℤ[1/p] (inclusion): H¹ = ℤ[1/p]/ℤ divisible with H¹[p] = ℤ/p, criterion fails; E_r⁰ = ℤ/p for all r while H⁰(M)[1/p] = 0.

tests.name: hatcher_bockstein_cohomology
tests.statement: A = ℤ, f = p, M integral singular cochains with finitely generated cohomology: E_2 is Hatcher's BHⁿ(X; ℤ/p) with the rules of Proposition 3E.3; E_∞ⁿ = (Hⁿ/torsion) ⊗ ℤ/p.
